title: PBW dimension and nilpotent augmentation for a Borel unipotent restricted algebra
statement: Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field of prime characteristic $p>0$ [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Let $S$ be a semisimple simply connected $F$-group scheme [def-sc-group-scheme]: smooth, connected, affine and of finite type, with no nontrivial smooth connected solvable normal subgroup, and such that every surjective homomorphism $S'\to S$ from a semisimple group scheme with finite central kernel is an isomorphism. Solvable means that iterated commutator subgroup schemes become trivial, and finite central means finite-dimensional coordinate algebra and commuting after every scalar extension. Fix a split maximal torus $T\subseteq S$ and a Borel subgroup $B\supseteq T$, with unipotent radical $U$, projection $\pi_T:B\to T$, character lattice $X=X^*(T)$, positive roots $\Phi^+$ in $\operatorname{Lie}(B)$, simple roots $\Delta$, and coroot pairing as in [lem-sfb-reductive-borel-pair-structure]. A split torus is a product of copies of $\mathbf G_m$; Borel means maximal smooth connected solvable closed subgroup, and the unipotent radical is the largest smooth connected normal unipotent subgroup, where unipotent means unipotent geometric matrices in a faithful representation. Put $Q=S/B$ and $N=|\Phi^+|$. Write $\mathfrak u=\operatorname{Lie}(U)$, the tangent space at the identity with bracket from commutators and restricted operation $x\mapsto x^{[p]}$ obtained by taking the $p$th iterate of the corresponding invariant derivation. Its restricted enveloping algebra $A=u(\mathfrak u)$ is the quotient of the tensor algebra $T_F(\mathfrak u)$ by $xy-yx-[x,y]$ and $x^p-x^{[p]}$. Its augmentation $\epsilon:A\to F$ sends $\mathfrak u$ to zero, and $J=\ker\epsilon$. Then $\dim_F A=p^N$ and there is an integer $h\ge1$ with $J^h=0$. A rational $U$-module is an $F$-vector space $W$ with a coaction $W\to W\otimes_F F[U]$ satisfying the counit and coassociativity identities. The algebra acts on such a module by differentiating its coaction; this action obeys $x^p=x^{[p]}$. The assertions allow $U=1$, in which case $A=F$ and $J=0$.

source.place: Section 1, restricted enveloping algebra definition, Theorem 1.2 and Corollary 1.3, printed pp.148--150; positive-root grading of the Borel radical in Section 1, printed pp.151--152. The nilpotent augmentation assertion is the bounded positive-root grading consequence, not a claim that x^[p] is always zero. WANTED: not stored in literature/. Read online at https://www.imsc.res.in/~knr/vdk/mathieu.pdf; all-characteristic semisimple version includes products of simple factors.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-reductive-borel-pair-structure] to the semisimple (hence reductive) group $S$: $B=U\rtimes T$. Apply [lem-sfb-regular-cocharacter-borel-description] to choose a regular cocharacter $\lambda$ with $B=P(\lambda)$ and $\operatorname{Lie}(B)=\operatorname{Lie}(T)\oplus\bigoplus_{\alpha\in\Phi^+}\mathfrak s_\alpha$, where $d_\alpha=\langle\alpha,\lambda\rangle>0$. On dual-number points, the product isomorphism $U\times T\simeq B$ identifies $\operatorname{Lie}(U)$ with the kernel of $d\pi_T$ and makes $d\pi_T$ the identity on $\operatorname{Lie}(T)$. Since $\pi_T$ commutes with conjugation by $T$ and conjugation on $T$ is trivial, $d\pi_T$ kills every nonzero character space: comparing Laurent monomials in the split-torus coordinates forces a linear map from character $\alpha\ne0$ to character zero to vanish. Thus $\mathfrak u=\bigoplus_{\alpha\in\Phi^+}\mathfrak s_\alpha$. By [lem-sfb-reductive-rank-one-reflections] each summand has dimension one. Choose $e_\alpha\ne0$ in each, in any order; these form an $N$-element basis.

source.place: Theorem 21.11(b)--(c), pp.428--429; Propositions 21.29, 21.31 and Theorem 21.32, pp.433--435; semidirect product in Theorem 16.33(d).

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-restricted-rational-differentiation], $\mathfrak u$ has the restricted operation used in the item, and conjugation by each $t\in T(F)$ preserves it. Therefore $t(e_\alpha^{[p]})=(\alpha(t)e_\alpha)^{[p]}=\alpha(t)^p e_\alpha^{[p]}$, so $e_\alpha^{[p]}$ has character $p\alpha$. By [lem-sfb-reductive-rank-one-reflections], the only roots rationally proportional to $\alpha$ are $\alpha$ and $-\alpha$; since $p\ge2$, $p\alpha$ is absent. Comparing characters in the direct sum from Step 1 gives $e_\alpha^{[p]}=0$. Similarly bracket preservation gives $[\mathfrak s_\alpha,\mathfrak s_\beta]\subseteq\mathfrak s_{\alpha+\beta}$, interpreted as zero when that character is absent. These are identities of torus characters, not their differentials, so remain valid in bad characteristic.

source.place: Paragraph preceding Proposition 11.36, p.223; Theorem 21.11(b)--(c), pp.428--429. Explicit character comparison in the restricted Lie algebra.

proof.text: Use [lem-sfb-restricted-pbw-basis] for the restricted Lie algebra $\mathfrak u$ and the ordered basis $e_\alpha$. Its monomials $\prod_\alpha e_\alpha^{a_\alpha}$ with $0\le a_\alpha<p$ are a basis of $A$. There are $p$ choices for each of its $N$ exponents, hence $\dim_F A=p^N$. The same theorem presents $A$ using only the basis commutator relations and $e_\alpha^p=e_\alpha^{[p]}=0$.

source.place: Theorem 10.40 and Corollary 10.41, p.207, including the basis-generator kernel assertion in the proof.

proof.text: Give the free words in the $e_\alpha$ degree $d_\alpha=\langle\alpha,\lambda\rangle$. Each commutator relation is homogeneous of degree $d_\alpha+d_\beta$, since $d_{\alpha+\beta}=d_\alpha+d_\beta$, and $e_\alpha^p=0$ is homogeneous of degree $pd_\alpha$. By the basis-generator presentation [lem-sfb-restricted-pbw-basis], these generate the whole relation ideal. That ideal is the span of products of words with these homogeneous relations; decomposing the words into their degrees makes each such product homogeneous. Consequently the quotient is a direct sum $A=\bigoplus_{d\ge0}A_d$ and $A_dA_e\subseteq A_{d+e}$. Its PBW basis is homogeneous, with degrees at most $D=(p-1)\sum_{\alpha\in\Phi^+}d_\alpha$. Hence $A_d=0$ for $d>D$ and $A_0=F\cdot1$.

source.place: Theorem 10.40, p.207: homogeneous use of its basis-generator presentation; agent-written positive-cocharacter grading argument.

proof.text: The map from the free algebra sending every $e_\alpha$ to zero kills the homogeneous defining relations, so factors through the augmentation $\epsilon:A\to F$ of the item. On the PBW basis it sends $1$ to $1$ and every other monomial to zero. Thus $J=\ker\epsilon=\bigoplus_{d>0}A_d$. Expand a product of $D+1$ elements of $J$ into its homogeneous terms. Every term has degree at least $D+1$, so vanishes by Step 4; finite sums of these products constitute $J^{D+1}$. Therefore $J^{D+1}=0$, with $h=D+1\ge1$. When $U=1$, the basis is empty, $N=D=0$, $A=F$, and this same calculation gives $J^1=0$.

source.place: Theorem 10.40, p.207, with the explicit graded-algebra augmentation calculation of Step 4; agent-written deduction.

proof.text: For any rational $U$-module $W$, apply [lem-sfb-restricted-rational-differentiation] to $H=U$ and its specified coaction. It yields $\rho(x)=(\operatorname{id}_W\otimes x)\alpha$, with $\rho([x,y])=[\rho(x),\rho(y)]$ and $\rho(x^{[p]})=\rho(x)^p$. The resulting action of $A$ is exactly differentiation of that coaction. This proves the module assertion without assuming $W$ finite-dimensional.

source.place: Section 10l, pp.207--208, interpreted by its coaction formula; restricted operation in the paragraph preceding Proposition 11.36, p.223.
